font-size: 18pt; line-height: 107%; mso-ansi-language: EN-IN; mso-highlight: yellow;\"\u003ESo the\nsamples of sputum and Bronchoalveolar Lavage that were sent for Microbiological\ninvestigations grew two different organisms E. coli and Klebsiella spp. That\nwere suggestive of \u0026nbsp;commensals. \u003Co:p\u003E\u003C\/o:p\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Cp class=\"MsoNormal\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cspan lang=\"EN-IN\" style=\"background: yellow; font-size: 18pt; line-height: 107%; mso-ansi-language: EN-IN; mso-highlight: yellow;\"\u003EAs far as\nthe diagnostic microbiology setup is concerned, we primarily base it on\nrepeated isolation, plausibility and the presence of the organism in large\nnumbers.\u003Cbr \/\u003E\nFor example in this patient we have seen that the primary pathology was an\norganised non resolving pneumonia. Pneumonia is\u0026nbsp;\nprimarily caused by pneumococci, staphylococci, haemophilus etc. \u003Co:p\u003E\u003C\/o:p\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Cp class=\"MsoNormal\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cspan lang=\"EN-IN\" style=\"background: yellow; font-size: 18pt; line-height: 107%; mso-ansi-language: EN-IN; mso-highlight: yellow;\"\u003ESo to\nisolate e coli from the sample raises questions as e coli being a primary pneumonic\npathogen is quite unheard of. \u003Co:p\u003E\u003C\/o:p\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Cp class=\"MsoNormal\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cspan lang=\"EN-IN\" style=\"background: yellow; font-size: 18pt; line-height: 107%; mso-ansi-language: EN-IN; mso-highlight: yellow;\"\u003EThe second\nthing is our correlation with the direct smear of the specimen. The number of\ngram negative bacilli were not quite high which doesn't quite agree with the\nisolated organism. However we also must remember that patient is on long term\nantibiotics\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u0026nbsp;Which would have contributed\nto further thinning of the organismal numbers. \u003Cbr \/\u003E\nKlebsiella is a feasible pathogen and it's isolation can be considered\nimportant. That's when we have to double check the other parameters such as the\npresence of pus cells and correlate with the direct smear. Klebsiella is also a\ncommensal which makes it even more confounding. So probably here the low\nnumbers of the organism in the direct smear coupled with a paucity of pus cells\ncontributes to the conclusion that the klebsiella is also not fitting into the\npathogen category\u003Co:p\u003E\u003C\/o:p\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Cp class=\"MsoNormal\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cspan lang=\"EN-IN\" style=\"background: yellow; font-size: 18pt; line-height: 107%; mso-ansi-language: EN-IN; mso-highlight: yellow;\"\u003EAnother\nimportant feature is the presence or absence of inflammatory cells. In this\ncase the inflammatory cells were very few on microscopy\u003Cbr \/\u003E\n, also no AFB was seen and we couldn't get sputum CBNAAT or mycobacterial\ncultures due to resource limitations and we tried ruling out viral etiologies in\nthis Pandemic for COVID19.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia;\"\u003EHere is a case i have seen:\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E27 y\/0 female arrived from West Bengal with chief complaints of Amenorrhea since 10 months and Multiple abortions.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;Patient got married in 2016, before marriage she used to have delayed or early menstruation by 3-4 days. After marriage(in 2016) she had Menstruation twice in one month and this reoccurred after 3 months. Between 2017-2018 in a span of 1 year she took oral contraceptive pills thrice ( Unwanted 72). The couple tried conceiving in 2018 and due to failed attempts visited a Gynaecologist in 2018 , she was advised medications for 2 months and then try conceiving . On follow-up after 2 months, the patient was asked to continue medications. Soon after that, In August 2019 she was tested pregnant 1st time and then they didn’t take the previous medicine prescribed. In October 2019 , she started bleeding per vaginal and underwent abortion and were advised to conceive 3 months later by the Gynaecologist.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn April 2020 she was tested pregnant again and after 2 months similar bleeding happened and underwent abortion.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAfter 1-1.5 months , she complained of Amenorrhea, and was tested for Pregnancy 3rd time. The couple denied that they didn’t try conceiving. However , they were told by the Gynaecologist that she was pregnant. After 1 month pervaginal bleed reoccured and was advised to undergo abortion. The couple refused and were prescribed Unwanted - KIT.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAfter 1 month she complained of Pain abdomen and visited an RMP. Following further investigations she was Suspected of gestational Trophoblastic disease and was started on injection Methotrexate on 29\/10\/2020 and on 2nd Line Actinomycin D on 11\/12\/2020.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe had also tested positive for IgG Rubella Virus and CMV.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe’s not a k\/c\/o HTN, DM or Thyroid diseases\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo c\/o allergies.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo significant family history, no history of Cancers in the family.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAppetite mixed , but decreased since 1 year. No addictions.\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"text-align: justify;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EInvestigations :\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u0026nbsp;USG Report\u003C\/div\u003E\u0026nbsp;
